fact: Cleopatra lived about 2,500 years after the Great Pyramid was built, but only about 2,000 years before Apollo 11. To her, the pyramids were already ancient.
The American Civil War began in 1861, 91 years after Captain Cook reached Australia's east coast and 110 years before the first email.
About 80 million years separate Stegosaurus and T. rex. That's more time than separates T. rex from you.
Woolly mammoths survived on Wrangel Island in the Arctic until around 2000 BC, after the Great Pyramid was built. That's closer to today than to Göbekli Tepe, one of the oldest known temples.
A close one: the Aztecs founded Tenochtitlan, on the site of today's Mexico City, in 1325, 119 years after Genghis Khan became Great Khan and 106 years before Joan of Arc was executed.

right: The Great Dying wipes out most life
fact: Sharks are older than trees. The oldest undisputed shark scales are about 420 million years old, while the first trees grew around 385 million years ago.
Sherlock Holmes first appeared in 1887, created by Edinburgh-born Arthur Conan Doyle. He's closer in time to Harry Potter than to Don Quixote.
Nintendo was founded in 1889 to make hand-made playing cards, 85 years after Napoleon crowned himself emperor.
Tetris was created in Moscow in 1984, five years before the Berlin Wall fell.

left: Karl Benz patents the motor car
fact: A close one: the first football World Cup, held in Uruguay in 1930, came 44 years after Karl Benz patented his motor car and 48 years before Space Invaders.
Machu Picchu looks ancient, but the Inca built it around 1450. That's much closer to today than to the building of the Parthenon in Athens.
Pluto was discovered in 1930, 61 years after Mendeleev drew up the periodic table, and counted as a planet for 76 years until 2006.
The original Grand Theft Auto was made in Dundee by DMA Design and released in 1997, seven years after Hubble launched and six years before the human genome was sequenced.
Roger Bannister ran the first mile in under four minutes in 1954, closer in time to Munch painting The Scream than to today.
A close one: the first recorded Olympics, in 776 BC, are slightly closer to the death of Socrates than to the death of Ramesses II.
Harvard was founded in 1636, closer in time to Louis XIV moving his court to Versailles than to Elizabeth I's coronation.
Big Ben first rang out in 1859, 16 years after Dickens's A Christmas Carol and 17 years before Edinburgh-born Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone.
The dodo was gone more than a century before the United States existed.
The Taj Mahal was finished around 1653, about 150 years after Leonardo began the Mona Lisa and roughly 170 years before Beethoven's Ninth Symphony was first performed.
A close one: Coca-Cola was invented in 1886, 21 years after the American Civil War ended and 19 years before Einstein's special relativity.
Teaching at Oxford began in 1096. Oxford is closer in time to you than to Hannibal crossing the Alps with his elephants.
Edison's practical light bulb arrived in 1879, 28 years after Moby-Dick and 29 years before the Model T.
Dinosaurs had been around for over 160 million years when the asteroid hit, about 66 million years ago. The end of their reign is closer to us than to its beginning.

left: Copernicus puts the Sun at the centre
right: Peter the Great founds St Petersburg
fact: The Mayflower landed in 1620, 77 years after Copernicus put the Sun at the centre of the universe and 83 years before St Petersburg was founded.

left: Van Gogh paints The Starry Night
fact: Mickey Mouse made his debut in Steamboat Willie in 1928, 39 years after Van Gogh painted The Starry Night and 49 years before Star Wars.
Pompeii was buried by Vesuvius in AD 79, roughly 800 years after Homer's Iliad is thought to have been written down.
Hero of Alexandria designed a coin-operated holy water dispenser in the 1st century AD, only about 260 years after Archimedes died.
Magna Carta was sealed in 1215, 415 years after Charlemagne was crowned emperor and 451 years before the Great Fire of London.

middle: The Beatles release their first album
fact: The Beatles released their first album, Please Please Me, in 1963, only 34 years after the first Academy Awards.

left: The Sony Walkman goes on sale
fact: A close call: YouTube launched in 2005, 26 years after the Sony Walkman first went on sale.
John Walker invented the friction match in 1826, 11 years after the Battle of Waterloo and 12 years before Queen Victoria was crowned.
For almost 50 years people opened tin cans with hammers and chisels. The dedicated can opener didn't appear until 1858.

right: The Game Boy goes on sale
fact: John Logie Baird, from Helensburgh in Scotland, gave the first public demonstration of television in 1926, 61 years after Alice in Wonderland was published.
The first Super Bowl was played in January 1967, 66 years after the first Nobel Prizes were awarded.

left: The Fosbury Flop wins Olympic gold
fact: A close call: Dolly, cloned at the Roslin Institute near Edinburgh, was born in 1996, 28 years after Dick Fosbury flopped his way to Olympic gold.
Insects had been around for well over 200 million years before the first flowers. Flowering plants are closer in time to you than to the first insects.

middle: The Epic of Gilgamesh is written down
fact: The Epic of Gilgamesh, one of the oldest known stories, was first written down around 2100 BC. That's closer to today than to the beginnings of farming.
Our species shared the planet with Neanderthals for well over 200,000 years before they disappeared, roughly 40,000 years ago.
The first apes appeared around 25 million years ago, long after the supercontinent Pangaea began to break apart.
China's Terracotta Army was buried around 210 BC with the First Emperor, about 110 years after Alexander the Great died.
Cambridge was founded in 1209, traditionally by scholars who left Oxford, 113 years after the First Crusade set out.
Galileo first turned a telescope to the sky in 1609, slightly closer in time to Handel's Messiah than to the Gutenberg Bible.
Basketball was invented in 1891 by James Naismith, a Canadian teacher in Massachusetts, 68 years after the first lighter.

left: The first voyage around the world ends
fact: Newton's Principia appeared in 1687, 165 years after the first voyage around the world ended and 172 years before Darwin's Origin of Species.

middle: The World Wide Web is invented
fact: A close one: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web in 1989, 14 years after Jaws and 13 years before euro notes and coins arrived.

middle: The Statue of Liberty is unveiled
fact: The Statue of Liberty was unveiled in New York in 1886, a gift from the people of France.
The first Tour de France was raced in 1903, 14 years after the Eiffel Tower opened and nine years before the Titanic sank.
Usain Bolt ran 100 metres in 9.58 seconds at the 2009 World Championships in Berlin, 23 years after the Chernobyl disaster.
Google was founded in 1998, 24 years after Muhammad Ali beat George Foreman in the Rumble in the Jungle.
The closest call of the day: Woodstock came 24 years after the Second World War ended and 25 years before the Channel Tunnel opened.

right: Most of today's Great Wall is built
fact: Hadrian's Wall was begun in AD 122, about 340 years after China's First Emperor unified the country. Most of the Great Wall you can visit today came much later, under the Ming dynasty.
The Roman Empire survived in the east until 1453, when the Ottomans took Constantinople. That's closer to today than to the Battle of Marathon.
The Ottoman Empire, founded around 1300, lasted until 1922. Its end is closer to the California Gold Rush than to today.
Tutankhamun died around 1323 BC, closer in time to the Phoenician alphabet than to Hammurabi's code of laws.
Leif Erikson's Vikings reached North America around the year 1000, slightly closer to Columbus than to the fall of the Western Roman Empire in 476.
Nicéphore Niépce took the oldest surviving camera photograph around 1826, about a century after Vivaldi's Four Seasons was published.
Nobody had seen Antarctica until 1820, 24 years after Edward Jenner gave the first vaccination.
The first Eurovision Song Contest was held in Switzerland in 1956, with just seven countries taking part.
Motorola's Martin Cooper made the first handheld mobile phone call in 1973, 24 years after Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four was published.
A close one: in 1896 Walter Arnold was fined for driving at 8mph in Kent, four times the speed limit, in what is often called the first speeding ticket.
Stonehenge's great sarsen stones went up around 2500 BC, about 700 years after writing first appeared in Mesopotamia.
The last Ice Age ended around 9700 BC, closer in time to the Lascaux cave paintings than to today.
The Colosseum in Rome opened in AD 80, about 150 years after Spartacus led his slave revolt.
Rome's legendary founding in 753 BC is closer to the traditional date of the Trojan War than to today.
A close one: the first coins were made in Lydia, in today's Turkey, around 600 BC. That's slightly closer to today than to the invention of the wheel.

middle: The Sistine Chapel ceiling is finished
fact: Michelangelo finished painting the Sistine Chapel ceiling in 1512, closer in time to Marco Polo's travels than to today.
Fry's of Bristol made the first moulded chocolate bar in 1847. Before that, chocolate was mostly a drink.
The world's first underground railway opened in London in 1863, with steam trains running through the tunnels.
Angkor Wat, built in the 1100s, is closer in time to Constantinople's Hagia Sophia, finished in 537, than to today.
Mozart was born in 1756, slightly closer to today than to the birth of Leonardo da Vinci.

left: People fly in a hot-air balloon
fact: Samurai were still fighting in 1877, slightly closer in time to the first heart transplant than to the first people flying in a hot-air balloon.

middle: Women first vote in a national election
fact: New Zealand became the first country to give women the vote in national elections, in 1893.
Bubble wrap was invented in 1957 by Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes, who were trying to make textured wallpaper. It didn't catch on as wallpaper.
The first text message, 'Merry Christmas', was sent in December 1992, 32 years after the first Paralympic Games in Rome.
Wikipedia launched in January 2001, 19 years after Michael Jackson's Thriller came out.
